summary: Repaired the constructor-replay experiment and recorded the account for its question. The first receipt (2d92d633d32a4a7c9e204b7dc5c8828b) carried the fixture operands and both construct results but the construct events omitted local_id, the identity field the comparisons use, so no admission could be matched to a result and all three comparisons returned unknown; that receipt is retained as an identity failure that establishes no comparison outcome, and its raw operands were deliberately not used. The successor adds the missing identity field and keeps the 9000-entry default-batch case while adding a 200-entry case with MaxAppendEntries=1, where 200 batches still exceed the 128-slot FSM mutation channel, so the trigger no longer depends on an entry gap above 8192; both feature-on cases have feature-off controls over identical fixtures. Local construction feedback was consistent across the four modes: both controls returned with lastApplied still at 1000 while both replay cases did not return within the 5s window, and an earlier all-noop variant returned in both modes, which is why the fixture uses LogCommand entries. The question-level interpretation is unresolved/unresolved: the mechanism is sourced (restoreFromCommittedLogs calls processLogs before the only consumer runFSM starts; fsmMutateCh holds 128 batches; entries are batched by MaxAppendEntries), but the fixture is harness-supplied, reachability of a 129- or 8193-entry committed-but-unapplied gap is argued from configurable SnapshotThreshold/MaxAppendEntries rather than observed, and no comparison has been evaluated yet. Incomplete: the successor receipt and its comparison interpretation, the no-feature restart control inside the cluster, the long-run persistence window, and whether a snapshot install eventually repairs the divergent same-term entries.
